section_title: What happens when we do not know how to pray?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 26 In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words. 27 And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.

context_lines: Creation groans, believers groan, and now Paul speaks of the Spirit’s help in their weakness. The setting is the long wait for bodily redemption. Not knowing how to pray belongs within that experience of limited understanding and hope.

The Spirit intercedes—He acts on believers’ behalf. God, who searches hearts, knows the Spirit’s mind, and the Spirit’s intercession agrees with God’s will. Paul locates the assurance in God’s knowledge and help, rather than in a person’s ability to find exactly the right words.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand these verses as reassurance that weakness in prayer does not leave believers without God’s help. Both [Calvin’s comments on verses 26–27](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/romans/8.htm) and [Wesley’s notes on those verses](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-epistle-to-the-romans/) connect the Spirit’s help with prayer directed toward God’s will. Their explanations differ in emphasis, but both place confidence in the Spirit’s work.
god_plan_lines: Paul also says in [Romans 8:34](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/8.htm) that the risen Christ intercedes for believers. Read together, the statements show God providing help through both the Son and the Spirit. The family relationship described earlier in the chapter includes help in the weakness of those who belong to Him.
current_position_lines: Our studies Prayer and Faith and What Does Prayer Look Like? understand these verses as an invitation to bring our weakness honestly before God. Prayer does not depend on perfectly formed requests. The Spirit helps where our understanding and words fall short, according to God’s will. We can trust Him without treating prayer as a way to secure a particular outcome.
